name: Jadoh
description: The best-known Khasi dish: rice, often red rice, cooked with pork and spices, sometimes with chicken or fish instead. It is traditionally served with dohkhlieh and tungrymbai, and roadside jadoh stalls at Mylliem near Shillong are famous for it.
how_to_eat: Eat with doh khlieh, tungtap chutney and a thin dal on the side.
how_to_order: Order a jadoh plate at a jadoh stall in Shillong's Lewdah (Bara Bazar) market or at Mylliem; you choose the meat side dish.

name: Dohkhlieh
description: A Khasi and Jaintia pork salad of boiled minced pork with onion, green chilli and salt; some places add tomato, beans or lemon. It is light, easy to make and sold at food stalls across the state.
how_to_eat: Eat as a side with jadoh or rice.
how_to_order: Ask for 'doh khlieh' at jadoh stalls and Khasi restaurants in Shillong.

name: Tungrymbai
description: Fermented soybeans of the Khasi and Jaintia peoples, cooked into a thick dish with black sesame, ginger, garlic, onion and often pork. It has a strong, earthy flavour; vegetarians can have it without the pork.
how_to_eat: Eat with hot steamed rice.
how_to_order: Ask for 'tungrymbai' with your jadoh or rice; ask if it has pork.

name: Doh Neiiong
description: Pork cooked with a paste of black sesame seeds, which gives a dark, nutty, earthy gravy. It is common in Khasi and Pnar (Jaintia) homes and is served at festivals.
how_to_eat: Eat with steamed rice or jadoh.
how_to_order: Ask for 'doh sniang nei-iong' (pork with black sesame) at Khasi restaurants.

name: Tungtap
description: A fermented fish paste of the Khasi and Garo, made from small barb fish that are sun-dried, salted and fermented in a sealed earthen pot. It is eaten as a very spicy chutney with onion, garlic and chilli; 'phan and tungtap' pairs it with boiled potatoes.
how_to_eat: Eat a small amount with rice, or with boiled potatoes (phan) and red tea.
how_to_order: Comes as a chutney with jadoh plates; ask for 'phan tungtap' at tea stalls.

name: Pumaloi
description: A Khasi steamed cake of powdered rice cooked in a black terracotta pot called khiew ranei. It is unspiced, so it is served with a gravy of pork, chicken or vegetables, at any meal of the day.
how_to_eat: Eat with a meat or vegetable curry.

name: Putharo
description: A soft, spongy rice-flour flatbread steamed in a special black pot. It is a Jaintia and Khasi favourite, paired with dohjem (pork curry with black sesame) or taken with tea and chutney.
how_to_eat: Eat with pork curry or with tea and chutney.

name: Pukhlein
description: A deep-fried Khasi rice cake of powdered rice and jaggery, thick and golden brown. It is one of the jingbam dihsha, the rice snacks served with red tea.
how_to_eat: Eat with tea as an evening snack.
how_to_order: Ask for 'pu khlein' at tea stalls and markets in Shillong.

name: Pusla
description: A Khasi rice cake steamed in a leaf, one of the jingbam dihsha rice snacks made from ground rice, water and sugar or jaggery.
how_to_eat: Eat with hot red tea.

name: Pudoh
description: A steamed Khasi rice cake with strips of pork inside. It is sold at the roadside jadoh stalls at Mylliem, south of Shillong.
how_to_eat: Eat warm with tea.

name: Ja Tyndong
description: Rice, fish, meat and vegetables cooked with water and spices inside fresh bamboo tubes sealed with banana leaf, then baked over fire until lightly charred. It is a rural Khasi farmers' dish.
how_to_eat: Split the bamboo and eat straight from it.

name: Ktung Bain Nei-iong
description: Ktung bain, a dry fish, cooked with black sesame seeds into a savoury, briny side dish. A Khasi accompaniment to rice.
how_to_eat: Eat with rice.

name: Doh Snam
description: A Khasi blood sausage of coarsely minced pork, offal and pork blood, wrapped and smoked; a variant stuffs pig intestines with herbed blood and tosses them with onion. It is found at stalls around Mylliem and Laitlyngkot.
how_to_eat: Eat with rice and chutney.

name: Doh Thad
description: Smoked pork fried with sliced onion and Naga chilli. A common side at Khasi roadside stalls.
how_to_eat: Eat with rice and chilli chutney.

name: Syiar Nei-iong
description: A Khasi chicken curry made with black sesame paste.
how_to_eat: Eat with rice.

name: Nakham Bitchi
description: A Garo soup or gravy of nakham, a sun- or fire-dried local fish, boiled with vegetables, chilli and pepper. It is spicy, prized as a delicacy and served as a starter before the main meal.
how_to_eat: Drink it as a starter or pour over rice.

name: Do'o Kapa
description: A Garo chicken curry cooked with kalchi, a natural potash that softens the meat, plus ginger, chilli and herbs. It is the everyday dish of most Garo homes.
how_to_eat: Eat with rice; fresh coriander and chilli are often added.

name: Wak Pura
description: A traditional Garo pork dish cooked with pura, a potash made by burning plant material or dried banana stems. The potash gives the pork a soft texture and mild alkaline note; spice is minimal.
how_to_eat: Eat with rice.

name: Me.kin (Sobok Chatni)
description: A Garo chutney made from banana flowers, served with most Garo meals.
how_to_eat: Eat a spoonful with rice.

name: Kharang
description: Smoked fish (dakharang) prepared by the Jaintia as a curry, chutney or salad, with a lingering smoky taste.
how_to_eat: Eat with rice.

name: Sakin Gata
description: A sweet sticky rice cake: rice soaked overnight, mixed with sugar, layered with roasted sesame, wrapped in banana leaf and steamed.
how_to_eat: Unwrap the leaf and eat as a dessert.
how_to_order: Found in local sweet shops across the state.

name: Shillong Aloo Muri
description: Shillong's cult street snack: chilled boiled potato with puffed rice, a spice mix, thinly chopped vegetables such as raw papaya and onion, and tamarind water. Vendors say it is unique to Shillong; a newer version adds Wai-Wai noodles.
how_to_eat: Eat it fresh from the vendor before the puffed rice goes soft.
how_to_order: Buy from street stands at Laitumkhrah Police Point or outside Lady Hydari Park; ask for more chilli or no onion as you like.

name: Kyat
description: A Khasi alcoholic drink of fermented rice boiled with water and local ingredients.
how_to_eat: Sip as a drink with food.
how_to_order: Available in bars and restaurants; Shillong is one of the best places to try it.

name: Cha Khoo
description: A Jaintia drink made from a rice concoction. It looks like tea but tastes mildly like coffee.
how_to_eat: Drink hot.

name: Sha Shiahkrot
description: A Khasi herbal tea made by boiling the root of the shiahkrot creeper (Smilax ferox).
how_to_eat: Drink hot like tea.
